# Portability corpora — structure-cloned from REAL peer installs, canary-substituted

Generated by `scripts/portability-corpus-gen.py`. **Do not hand-edit.** Regenerate with:

```bash
python3 scripts/portability-corpus-gen.py --source ~/.hermes   --kind hermes   --out hermes
python3 scripts/portability-corpus-gen.py --source ~/.openclaw --kind openclaw --out openclaw
```

## What these are

The authoritative automated gate for phase 26 runs on Linux, but the only real-world-scale peer
installs live on the planning Mac and hold live provider credentials. Those credentials must never
cross a host boundary. So each corpus reproduces a real peer tree's **shape** — the same relative
paths, file names, file formats and key identities — while every value classified as a secret is
replaced by a distinct canary token.

Each corpus carries a `MANIFEST.json` recording the classification rules, the observed counts, and
every canary token with the file and key path it sits at. **Gates read the canary list from that
manifest at run time.** No canary is hard-coded in a source file or in a plan, so a regenerated
corpus does not silently invalidate a test.

## These are realism fixtures, not adversarial ones

The corpus reproduces what a real install looks like. It is deliberately NOT a hostile corpus —
symlink escapes, `..` components, case collisions and oversized files are 26-04's subject.

## Bounded, by design

`MANIFEST.json` sets `bounded: true`. A real Hermes home measures 2.0 GB (540 skill directories plus
image/audio caches, logs and sessions); cloning it verbatim is not committable and adds no
discriminating power. Importer-relevant files are cloned verbatim; every other tree is reproduced as
**directory markers** — each real subdirectory becomes an empty directory holding a `.keep`, so a
counter still observes the real shape. Measured: 12 profiles × 45 skill directories = 540, matching
the real install exactly.

## Provenance of the committed corpora

| Corpus | Files | Canaries | Cloned from |
|---|---|---|---|
| `hermes/` | 581 | 36 | real `~/.hermes` — 12 profiles, 1 MCP server, 540 skill dirs, 12 `SOUL.md` |
| `openclaw/` | 19 | 28 | real `~/.openclaw` — 10 config files incl. 8 backup/last-good siblings, 2 credential files |

Both were proven byte-identical across two generator runs, and a search for the 7 real secret values
extracted from the two real homes returned **zero hits** across every committed file.
